chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about men who shared in a slave girl, so they entrusted one of them with the stipulation that the slave girl would be with him, so he copulated with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Part of the legal punishment (Hadd) is staved off from him by the measure of what is for him in her from the cash, and he is whipped by the measure of what is not for him in her; and the slave girl is evaluated upon him with a price and it is binding upon him. And if the evaluation is less than the price with which the girl was bought, her former price is obligated. And if her evaluation on that day in which she was evaluated is more than her price, that price is obligated, and he is belittled because he bedded her.' I said, 'And if one of the partners wishes to buy her apart from the man?' He said: 'That is for him, and it is not for him that he buys her until he exonerates her, and it is not upon someone else that he buys her except with the price.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who has intercourse with a shared slave girl?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudence of joint ownership (shirkah) in female slaves, specifically addressing the reduction of the Hadd punishment for unlawful intercourse based on the perpetrator's financial share. It further clarifies the valuation mechanism for compensation, ensuring that partners are reimbursed according to the slave's market value at the time of the act, regardless of whether it exceeds or falls short of the original purchase price. This ruling underscores the practical application of property rights and liability distribution within Shia fiqh.
